Marissa / team,

Quick triage notes (first 30m):
- Correlation: spike coincides with Brightline marketing blast at 17:28 PT — inbound QPS ~3x baseline for ~20m.
- Observed metrics (17:28–17:55 window): hosted-chat-sse p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.35s (stable baseline p99 ~270–330ms). 5xx rate increased to ~1.8% (primarily 502/504 upstream timeouts).
- Root cause hypothesis: a combination of (A) per-connection CPU/KV-cache churn on hot KV prefixes increasing tail, and (B) autoscaler reaction lag + scheduler fragmentation causing temporary under-provisioning on the GPU worker pool. We also see increased time in request queuing for long-lived SSE handshake routes.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (minutes -> hours):
1) Short term (now): enable fast-fallback routing for Brightline to a quantized model variant and increase target pool size by +30% for the evening window (manual scale). This reduces per-token CPU and should lower p99 quickly.
2) Clear KV cache warm paths: pre-warm top prefixes for Brightline's traffic (we can push a cache seed within 20m).
3) If autoscaler still lagging, temporarily relax min-available-to-scale threshold for the SSE worker group to scale more aggressively.

Planned next steps:
- I'm attaching an RCA timeline with metric slices (rca-timeline.csv) and a screenshot of the p99 graph (metrics-screenshot.png).
- Estimate: we can get p99 back under 450ms within ~25–40 minutes after pool bump + fallback routing. Full fix (autoscaler heuristics + kernel-level KV optimization) is a 6–36 hour story depending on rollout cadence.

I'll execute the pool bump now pending Marissa/ops approval and will coordinate a 30m roll call if needed.

—Rishi
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
